title: SOA vs Demat for MFs: SEBI's New Rule & Your Choice
description: SEBI has recently allowed standing instructions for Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plans (STP) on mutual fund units held in demat a.

faq.q: What is a Statement of Account (SOA) for mutual funds?
faq.a: An SOA is a physical or electronic record issued by a mutual fund house or its Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) confirming your ownership of mutual fund units. It's a direct way to hold units without a demat account.

A demat account holds your securities, including shares, bonds, and mutual fund units, in an electronic format. It's maintained by a Depository Participant (DP) and provides a consolidated view of all your electronic holdings.

faq.q: What was SEBI's recent move regarding demat accounts and mutual funds?
faq.a: SEBI recently allowed Depository Participants (DPs) to offer standing instruction facilities for Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWP) and Systematic Transfer Plans (STP) for mutual fund units held in demat accounts. This automates these transactions for demat holders.

faq.q: Are demat accounts mandatory for investing in mutual funds?
faq.a: No, demat accounts are not mandatory for investing in mutual funds. You can still hold mutual fund units directly with the fund houses through a Statement of Account (SOA).

faq.q: Can I convert my existing SOA-held mutual fund units into demat form?
faq.a: Yes, you can dematerialise your SOA-held mutual fund units by submitting a dematerialisation request form (DRF) to your Depository Participant (DP). The process typically involves submitting your physical or electronic SOA units for conversion.

faq.q: Which option is generally cheaper: SOA or demat for mutual funds?
faq.a: Generally, holding mutual funds via SOA (especially direct plans) can be cheaper as it avoids the Annual Maintenance Charges (AMC) and potential transaction fees associated with a demat account. However, the overall cost depends on the demat account charges and whether you invest in direct or regular plans.
